title: Decide every browser.session request on the browser target, refuse writes to signed origins unless the founder signs them, and keep the step program a founder-signed literal
problem: browser.session is declared internal_write (greg/capabilities.py), but on base a6c29bbd its allow() handler (greg/computer.py:163-168) checked only the origin and continued any HTTP method to a signed origin. With browser discovery fixed, an unmarked click on a POST form delivered POST /order to the loopback server (count 1), the session returned COMPLETED and the order page was extracted. That is a consequence-gate bypass, a kill criterion in directive section 67. greg/pipeline.py PROTECTED also omitted the step fields, so an earlier action's untrusted output could bind the whole step program. And the computer-use suite was invisible: tests/unit/test_greg_computer.py skipped as a whole module ('no Chromium installed'), even with Playwright installed, because computer.chromium() looked only in chrome-linux/ and the preinstalled build lives in chrome-linux64/.
founder_intent_refs: INTENT-20261028-OPUS-MAXIMUS-REISSUE, sections 31 (computer use), 34 (hostile input), 35 (generated code is untrusted), 36 (zero trust), 67 (kill criteria: permits consequence-gate bypass)
INTENT-GREG-EMBODIED-2026-09-11 (authorized computer use on the first body)
baseline: a6c29bbd (#196 head): allow() continues any method to a signed origin; allow_socket() refuses only unsigned origins; the consequential marker on a step is a declaration, not a mechanism; PROTECTED lacks op, selector, secret, consequential and a step-program rule; requirements, installer and CI install no Playwright, and test_greg_computer.py (8 tests) and the confined browser test importorskip it.

alternatives.name: Proposed: browser-target request interception, channel removal, signed read_methods exceptions and a protected step program
alternatives.description: CDP Fetch enabled on the browser target before the context exists pauses every request of every page, frame and worker, including unload-time requests and each redirect hop; HTTP is decided only there, against the origin bound and the method gate (GET, HEAD and OPTIONS without a body pass; anything else, and any WebSocket, needs a signed read_methods entry naming method, origin and exact path). Channels no interception sees are removed in two layers: --disable-blink-features=WebSocketStream,SharedWorker and a page prelude deleting Worker, SharedWorker, WebSocketStream, WebTransport, RTCPeerConnection, webkitRTCPeerConnection and Navigator.prototype.serviceWorker in every frame. Any refused write ends the session at AUTHORITY_BOUNDARY with the original stop in the reason, including one seen at close. pipeline.resolve refuses a $from_action at the params root, at a bound steps list or a whole step, and at op, selector, secret, consequential and read_methods; a fill value and an integer steps still bind. The suite runs: chromium() finds chrome-linux64, playwright==1.63.0 is pinned, GREG_REQUIRE_BROWSER=1 turns a missing Playwright into a failure, and a new workflow runs the suites and 26 mutants.
advantages: Measured on the unmarked POST-form probe: POST /order count 1 and COMPLETED before; 0 and AUTHORITY_BOUNDARY after, with blocked_methods {'POST 127.0.0.1:<port>/order': 1}
Every reviewer probe that delivered a write on 7b7ea61e delivers none on cebf1674 (server writes [] everywhere)
Commodity mechanisms only: Playwright, the Chrome DevTools Protocol Fetch domain, a Blink feature flag and an init script; no new authority plane
test_greg_computer.py goes from a module skip to 35 tests that run against a real Chromium; 26/26 mutants caught
disadvantages: The gate sees methods, not effects: a GET with side effects or data in a GET query to a signed origin is not detected
Channel removal by the page prelude is page-script level, as strong as Playwright's own WebSocket mock and no stronger
Pages that need a worker lose it; same-origin telemetry writes, including at close, end the session unless the founder signs that exact endpoint
The gate lives only in the browser; the confined relay still checks origins only
alternatives.revival_evidence: Retained; revisit when a method-aware egress point below the browser exists, or when a channel or realm is found that bypasses the browser-target interception or the prelude.

roles.position: Directive sections 34 and 36 require that external content cannot authorize consequential action and that bypass is prevented or detectable; section 67 names consequence-gate bypass as a kill criterion. This unit replaces the bypass with a mechanism and records every refusal. It is built under INTENT-20261030-BUILD-BEFORE-DEVICE-RUN: no founder-device run, and no claim beyond INTEGRATION-TESTED.
material_concerns: 'Consequence comes from mechanism' holds for HTTP methods and the removed channels, not for a GET with side effects; it must not be presented as complete
Section 31 keeps broad computer use as a destination: pages that lose workers are a narrowing of today's capability, not of the destination, and stay on the horizon

pass_2.attack_summary: Two adversarial reviews by separate agents of this session attacked the first-round head 7b7ea61e as deployed: one for bypasses of the method gate and step-program rule, one for fidelity of the claims. They reported 16 findings (F1-F10, WU10-R1..R6) plus an info finding (R7). All 16 were reproduced with the reviewers' own probes, then fixed in 661602d0, 1b4eedc8 and cebf1674; the fixes were checked by rerunning those probes and a final verification, not by a third review. Preparing this record added one attack: a merge with open #209.

residual_risks.risk: A GET with side effects, or data in a GET query, reaches a signed origin
residual_risks.mitigation: Stated in every trace (method_gate) and the docstring; founder decision before browser.act

residual_risks.risk: A realm the prelude does not reach reopens worker, WebTransport or WebRTC channels
residual_risks.mitigation: Engine flags cover WebSocketStream and SharedWorker; a below-browser gate is the next stage
residual_risks.review_trigger: Any such realm found, or a Chromium upgrade

residual_risks.risk: Founder burden rises from refused telemetry writes and worker-dependent pages
residual_risks.mitigation: Exact signed exceptions; the trade-off is a founder decision
residual_risks.review_trigger: First real mission blocked this way

residual_risks.risk: The #209 conflict is resolved by taking #209's side of pipeline.inspect(), which this branch's depth-0 rule then refuses
residual_risks.mitigation: Exact resolution recorded; test_greg_pipeline_protected.py and #209's tests must pass on the merged tree
residual_risks.review_trigger: Intake of #209 or of this PR, whichever is second

residual_risks.risk: The workflow fails on a hosted runner (non-root Chromium sandbox, bubblewrap)
residual_risks.mitigation: It is a separate workflow; a failure blocks nothing in Canonical CI and is the evidence to act on

dissent.handling: Recorded with thresholds; neither entry blocks the draft, and either blocks browser.act or wider autonomy if its threshold is met.

entries.position: A gate that lives only in the browser is one unreached realm away from bypass; before browser.act or wider autonomy, a method-aware egress point below the renderer must also refuse writes.
entries.rationale: The prelude is page-script level and WebTransport was not exercised end to end; the relay checks origins only.
entries.evidence_threshold: Any channel that delivers a non-read request or a WebSocket to a signed origin without passing the browser-target interception, or any realm the prelude does not reach
entries.review_trigger: Before browser.act, or the first such channel found

entries.position: Removing workers, WebRTC and WebTransport from every page and ending sessions on telemetry writes should be measured on real sites before adoption; the safety gain may cost founder attention.
entries.rationale: Directive section 67 also kills architecture that increases founder burden without sufficient gain; only loopback pages were measured.
entries.evidence_threshold: A real founder mission that stops at AUTHORITY_BOUNDARY on a telemetry write or fails for a missing Worker
entries.review_trigger: First real browser.session mission after intake

migration_plan: No data migration. browser.session gains one optional founder-signed param (read_methods) and trace fields (blocked_methods, read_methods_used, method_gate, a close record); existing missions keep working unless they bind a whole params, a steps list or step, or op, selector, secret, consequential or read_methods through $from_action, which none found does. kill_criteria: Any non-read request or WebSocket from a browser.session page reaches a signed origin without a signed read_methods entry and without the session ending at AUTHORITY_BOUNDARY
Any request to an unsigned origin leaves the browser
A refused write is reported with any other status, or goes unrecorded
An earlier action's output sets a capability's whole params, a step program, a whole step, or a step's op, selector, secret, consequential or read_methods
With GREG_REQUIRE_BROWSER=1, a missing Playwright skips instead of failing
The narrowing raises founder burden on real missions without a matching safety gain (directive section 67)
